originalResponses.title: Start the AI working log immediately
Begin the two-section note and static review in parallel
Respect and summarize the fictional context
Resolve and raise Dana's conflicting requests
Give the product build order, rough estimates and first cut
End Dana's section with testable acceptance criteria
Write the storage and scale decisions with reasons
Explain enforcement of all eight house rules
Preserve the supplied data-model meanings and constraints
Build the trend and access-log client views
Make the client accessible as required
Review all eight supplied PR files statically
Check the review's evidence and scope
Run ingestion and retention tests on our own build
Run the access matrix and confidentiality tests
Verify hidden/missing and clinical boundary behaviour
Perform our chosen small backup/restore check
Finalize the AI working log and included history
Freeze features and assemble the final package
Confirm delivery details and inspect access
Draft the exact submission reply together
B01: Proxy confidentiality depends on a fixed list of encounter IDs
B02: Patient reads do not check clinician release or critical handling
B03: The total reveals observations removed from the page
B04: The denial path creates and logs patient-identifying information
B05: A clinical response can succeed without its audit
B06: Denied attempts never reach the audit writer
B07: Conversion uses display text, and the eGFR path bypasses it
B08: The eGFR formula mixes versions and includes a race multiplier
B09: The per-minute result is not converted to the advertised per-second unit
B10: The calculator accepts unsuitable inputs and hides failure reasons
B11: Historical results are interpreted using today's demographics
B12: One age-14 switch applies to every analyte
B13: A missing range is returned as NORMAL
B14: The mapper assumes every result has one scalar value
B15: Correction writes delete the original
B16: Dynamic search interpolates values into SQL
B17: A small page still loads and decodes the entire history
B18: The declared return type cannot accept the result of round
B19: The routes do not match the required URLs
B20: Both clinical classes name the wrong R4 gender enum
B21: Clinical meaning changes with coding order
B22: Writes store a reference while reads use a patient key
B23: A qualified value is turned into an exact measurement
B24: Equal-time results can move between pages
P01: Remove unused wiring and correct the comments
P02: Remove or deliberately support optional sort
V02: Put revocation and reads under a declared snapshot
V03: Specify accepted effective-time and request forms
V05: Define status eligibility and derived provenance

contributionsThroughCodex.contribution: Provided the job description, invitation, attachments, startup/adviser impression, reported Flutter/Spring Boot/AWS/Rust stack, and the first-interview device/edge/security/reliability scenario. These inputs shaped the analysis; fictional Aldercrest facts remained separate.

Explicitly selected AI-written code with candidate decision review and verification, requested assistance at every step, required no guessing and primary-source checking, and required defensible engineering/privacy/security practices throughout delivery.

Selected isolated tools, the existing LyveMD workspace, private repository name, plain same-service HTML/CSS/JavaScript client and configured commit-author email. Chose EDB PostgreSQL rather than the proposed alternative and supplied the downloaded EDB ZIP.
Required meaningful commits and private pushes for every meaningful change, task-completion announcements, ordered group execution, updated estimates and progress/stall reporting.

Adopted the AI-drafted exact access instruction and Packages A/B, choosing the stated ingestion, replay/correction, access-log, time/context, release and audit policies. Draft authorship remains AI; actual adoption is the candidate decision.

Asked for reasoning before deciding ambiguous issues, then adopted derived-only BMI/eGFR input, the 1 March age convention, HTTPS extension identifiers, identical unavailable POST-reference errors, one-way clinical workflow, patient-self proxy revocation, retained/derived trend conventions, the 100-patient/about-10k dataset and disclosed synthetic terminology handling.
Personally reported the two displayed 11.5 g/dL haemoglobin results: 30 June 2026 range11–14/Normal and 1 July range12–15.5/Low.
Personally reported weight74kg and BMI cannot compute/height unavailable, the matching no-point chart and exact-value table, and visible focus/Tab/Enter working on the trend controls.

Personally reported sodium trend94points before filtering and10 for the stated2026window. Reported STAFF allowed log/denied results and assigned CLINICIAN allowed results/denied log, including the observed normal sodium140mmol/L.

Requested a deeper full static review and an accurately scoped joint walkthrough, participated in the written/chat explanation, and requested more natural report wording. The later form adds the separate independent/partial static reviews listed below.

Explicitly deferred further manual client checks to prioritize delivery, requested an explanation of audit-failure behavior, then later reported the independent submission walkthrough and itemized repository reviews outside Codex.
Reported the interview slot reserved and relevant transcripts submitted; clarified that the assignment is not yet submitted and that the candidate will send it manually.
